title: DROP DATABASE
description: Learn how to delete a database in SQL Server using the DROP DATABASE statement.

data.text: The DROP DATABASE statement removes an existing database from a SQL Server instance, including all its data and physical disk files.

data.title: DROP DATABASE Syntax
data.content: Drops one or more databases, optionally using IF EXISTS to avoid errors.

data.text: Key points about the DROP DATABASE statement:

items: Specify the name of the database to drop after the DROP DATABASE keyword.
Use a comma-separated list to drop multiple databases in a single statement.
The IF EXISTS option (available from SQL Server 2016) conditionally drops the database only if it exists, preventing errors for non-existent databases.
The DROP DATABASE statement deletes the database and its physical disk files. Always ensure you have a backup before dropping a database.
You cannot drop a database that is currently in use.

data.title: Important
data.text: Dropping a database permanently deletes all its data and physical files. Always back up the database before dropping it.

data.title: DROP DATABASE Key Points
points: Use DROP DATABASE to remove a database and its physical files.
Use IF EXISTS to avoid errors when the database may not exist.
You can drop multiple databases in a single statement.
Always back up a database before dropping it.
You cannot drop a database that is currently in use.
